label: Target population: mechanism, not expression
text: PITFALL: Defining 'SV-driven TXR1 activation' by high TXR1 expression, or by any reported junction, mixes in non-driving SVs and lineage-driven high expression; most SVs near a gene do not change its expression, and only promoter-facing enhancer-hijack rearrangements activate it. CHECK: Cross-tabulate breakpoint_topology (P2T vs INV/D2T/NONE) against txr1_log_tpm, lineage_marker_log_tpm, target_ase_alt_fraction and phase_consistency; see whether high-TXR1 non-P2T cases are explained by lineage expression or copy number. IF FOUND: Define the target population from mechanism-consistent multi-modal evidence (P2T topology + adequate alt_molecule_fraction + haplotype-consistent ASE/phase), not from expression level alone; report sensitivity to the definition. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-05504-4 ; https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkae646.

label: Long-read SV artifacts in repeats
text: PITFALL: Long-read SV calls at loci with segmental duplication, high homology or low complexity are often false positives from mis-mapping to paralogous copies, so some reported P2T junctions may be artifacts. CHECK: Look at the distribution of mapq_median, segmental_dup_overlap, homology_bp, low_complexity_score, split_molecule_count, molecule_depth and read_n50 among P2T calls, by platform; flag P2T calls with low MAPQ or high SD overlap that lack expression/ASE/phase support. IF FOUND: Treat artifact-prone calls as not SV-driven (or analyse them as uncertain, with sensitivity analyses including or excluding them) instead of trusting the topology label. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-022-01457-8 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7641771/.

label: Purity/copy-number confound allelic evidence
text: PITFALL: Raw allele fractions (alt_molecule_fraction, target_ase_alt_fraction) are diluted by low tumor purity and distorted by local copy-number gain or WGD, so a true clonal SV in a low-purity sample can look weak, and amplification can raise TXR1 or mimic allelic imbalance without any SV. CHECK: Plot alt_molecule_fraction and ASE fraction against tumor_purity, local_total_copy, tumor_ploidy and wgd_flag; check whether high TXR1 expression in non-P2T cases tracks local_total_copy. IF FOUND: Purity/copy-adjust the fractions (expected fraction about purity*mutant copies/total copies) before applying any threshold, so that low-purity true SVs are not excluded; do not count amplification-only activation as SV-driven. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7985293/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6778654/.

label: Missing week-16 outcome: hypothetical estimand
text: PITFALL: A complete-case analysis of week-16 benefit (dropping assessed16==0) is biased when non-assessment depends on prognosis or on treatment toxicity; early toxicity discontinuation is a likely cause of missing week-16 visits under TXR1i. CHECK: Tabulate assessed16 by therapy_class, tox_stop_8wk, ecog, tumor_burden, site and calendar_period; fit a model for P(assessed16=1 | treatment, baseline covariates). IF FOUND: The estimand 'as if all had an assessable week-16 visit' is a hypothetical estimand: estimate it with inverse-probability-of-missingness weights multiplied by treatment weights, or with g-computation/AIPW (doubly robust), under MAR given the covariates; state that this assumption cannot be tested and run a sensitivity analysis (delta/tipping-point). Do not impute non-assessed as failure, which is a composite estimand and not the one asked for. SOURCE: https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/E9%2DR1_Step4_Guideline_2019_1203.pdf ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10228513/.

label: Confounding and positivity diagnostics
text: PITFALL: Registry treatment choice is confounded (ECOG, tumor burden, prior lines/resistance, lineage, site, calendar period), and in the target population nearly everyone may have received TXR1i, so IPW gives extreme weights or the comparison is unsupported by data. CHECK: Within the target population, check propensity score overlap by arm, max/min weights, effective sample size and weighted standardized mean differences (<0.1) for all baseline confounders; look for structural non-positivity (e.g. a site or period with no SYS patients). IF FOUND: Use a doubly robust estimator, report the region with overlap, and say explicitly if trimming or overlap weights move the estimand away from the full target population; never trim silently. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8492528/ ; https://academic.oup.com/aje/article/188/1/250/5090958.

label: Target trial alignment at time zero
text: PITFALL: Restricting to outside analysis_set, or using covariates or outcomes measured after treatment start, breaks the target trial: eligibility, assignment and time zero must line up, or selection and immortal-time bias follow. Adjusting for post-baseline variables such as assessed16 or toxicity opens collider bias. CHECK: Use only analysis_set==1 as the time-zero cohort; check time_zero_day and that every covariate is baseline; never put tox_stop_8wk into the treatment or benefit confounder set. IF FOUND: Keep only baseline confounders in the treatment model; handle post-baseline events through the missingness model, not through eligibility. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5124536/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12927355/.

label: DLR1 activity score and marginal toxicity
text: PITFALL: Toxicity under TXR1i probably depends on germline DLR1 metabolizer status; treating each star allele as a separate category, or ignoring low-confidence diplotype calls, misrepresents that risk. Because the requested toxicity risk is a marginal risk under TXR1i in the whole target population, a crude rate among TXR1i-treated patients is biased if their DLR1 or clinical makeup differs from the whole target population. CHECK: Compute activity score = sum of the two haplotype activity values from dlr1_allele_table; tabulate tox_stop_8wk by activity score under TXR1i; check dlr1_call_confidence and ancestry_group. IF FOUND: Estimate the 8-week toxicity risk under TXR1i by standardizing (g-computation or IPW) over the whole target population's covariate distribution, including activity score; handle low-confidence calls through a sensitivity analysis or multiple imputation. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6951851/ ; https://pharmcat.clinpgx.org/methods/Matching-Recommendations/.

label: Batch/lineage and subgroup misclassification
text: PITFALL: Expression features (txr1_log_tpm, ASE) can be shifted by expression_batch, rna_quality and library size, and TXR1 baseline expression correlates with the lineage program, so fixed expression cut-offs misclassify cases; misclassifying who belongs to the biomarker subgroup biases the subgroup effect toward the effect in the misclassified group, usually toward the null. CHECK: Compare txr1_log_tpm and housekeeping_log_tpm across expression_batch and rna_quality; regress TXR1 on lineage_marker_log_tpm to obtain lineage-adjusted residual expression; check how stable subgroup membership is under alternative definitions. IF FOUND: Normalize within batch and use lineage-adjusted expression only as supporting evidence; report effect estimates under the stricter and the looser definitions of the subgroup. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4107031/ ; https://doi.org/10.1111/rssc.12364.

label: Marginal RD in target population
text: PITFALL: The TXR1i benefit is likely concentrated in true SV-driven tumors (effect modification), so an estimate over the full registry, or one conditional on covariates (such as a logistic odds ratio), is not the requested marginal risk difference in the target population. CHECK: Estimate the effect in the target group and in non-target groups separately; make sure the reported number is a standardized marginal risk difference in percentage points. IF FOUND: Fit the models within the target population, or include interactions, and marginalize over the target population's covariates; use bootstrap CIs that repeat the whole pipeline (missingness weights, propensity, outcome, toxicity) and propagate uncertainty into net utility = RD - 0.35*toxicity risk. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4052139/.

label: Tract-length rate is t(1-m), not t
text: PITFALL: Using t = 1/(mean tract length) ignores invisible within-ancestry recombination; under a single pulse t generations ago with ancestry-A fraction m, tracts of ancestry A are exponential with rate t*(1-m) per Morgan (not t), and B tracts with rate t*m, so the naive estimator is biased by a factor 1/(1-m) and badly wrong when m is far from 0.5. CHECK: estimate t separately from A tracts and from B tracts on the same haplotype using rate=t*(1-m) and rate=t*m; the two must agree, and compare against the naive 1/mean which will not. IF FOUND: estimate t jointly, e.g. t = S / (2*m*(1-m)*L) where S is the number of observed ancestry switches and L the total called span in Morgans, or equivalently t = 1/(mean_A_length*(1-m)). SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05904 and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374321/

label: Censoring at chromosome and span ends
text: PITFALL: Tracts that touch the start or end of a chromosome or of the called span are right-censored (truncated), so treating their observed length as a complete tract shortens the mean and inflates t. CHECK: per chromosome and haplotype, count how many segments begin at the first called coordinate or end at the last called coordinate, and what fraction of total A span they hold; compare mean length of boundary versus interior tracts. IF FOUND: use the censored exponential MLE, rate = (number of uncensored tract ends) / (total Morgan span of all tracts of that ancestry, censored ones included in the denominator); equivalently count ancestry switches as events and total span as exposure. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8557420/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374321/

label: Spurious short low-confidence segments
text: PITFALL: Spurious very short segments from local-ancestry inference error (low posterior, repeat or low-complexity regions) add fake ancestry switches, inflate t, and make a non-exponential length distribution look exponential. CHECK: tabulate segment length against the posterior and low_complexity_frac columns and look for an excess of segments below about 1-2 cM concentrated at low posterior or high low_complexity_frac. IF FOUND: drop segments failing a posterior threshold (for example below 0.9) or with high low_complexity_frac (for example above 0.5), remove their span from the denominator rather than counting them as switches, and report how sensitive t is to the threshold. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374321/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9943733/

label: Merge adjacent same-ancestry tracts
text: PITFALL: After filtering or across gaps, adjacent segments of the same ancestry left unmerged are counted as two tracts separated by a switch, which roughly doubles the inferred switch rate. CHECK: scan the segment list per chromosome and haplotype for consecutive rows carrying the same anc label, and for same-ancestry pairs that flank a dropped or uncalled interval. IF FOUND: merge them into one tract, summing length and excluding any uncalled interval from the span, before any likelihood or mean-length calculation. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374321/

label: Interchromosomal phase: h1/h2 may not be one parent
text: PITFALL: Haplotype labels h1 and h2 are assigned independently per chromosome, so they need not correspond to the same parent genome-wide (interchromosomal phase ambiguity); pooling chromosomes under mislabelled haplotypes pulls both parental A-fractions toward the genome-wide mean and shortens apparent tracts, so the parental difference is understated and t overstated. CHECK: compute the per-chromosome A-fraction for h1 minus h2 and see whether the sign is consistent across chromosomes; inconsistent signs with large magnitudes indicate label swapping, whereas a consistent sign supports genome-wide-consistent labels. IF FOUND: resolve labels per chromosome (for example by assigning each chromosome's haplotypes so as to maximise the between-haplotype A-fraction separation), note that this choice biases the estimated difference upward, and cross-check with an unphased, homozygosity-based estimate of the two parental fractions. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9388397/ and https://doi.org/10.1093/g3journal/jkaf122

label: Switch errors appear as coincident breakpoints
text: PITFALL: A phasing switch error inside a chromosome looks exactly like a real ancestry switch and appears as two coincident, opposite ancestry breakpoints on h1 and h2 at the same coordinate, which inflates the switch count on both haplotypes and biases t upward while mixing the two parents' ancestry fractions. CHECK: list breakpoint coordinates for h1 and h2 per chromosome and flag positions where both haplotypes switch at the same Morgan coordinate in opposite directions (A-to-B on one, B-to-A on the other). IF FOUND: treat it as a phase error, flip the downstream haplotype assignment to restore the longer tracts, and recompute; if the pattern is frequent, prefer a phase-free or unphased estimator of the parental fractions and times. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1093/g3journal/jkaf122 and https://doi.org/10.1002/cpz1.70321

label: Length-weighted fraction over called span only
text: PITFALL: The ancestry-A fraction must be Morgan-length-weighted over the span actually called, not a count of segments and not a physical-position or whole-chromosome denominator; the called tract span can be shorter than the chromosome lengths given in map_info.tsv, and using chromosome length as the denominator deflates both fractions. CHECK: for each haplotype sum the segment lengths per chromosome and compare with length_morgan in map_info.tsv to quantify uncalled flanks and interior gaps; verify the two haplotypes cover the same span. IF FOUND: set the denominator to the sum of retained, called segment lengths in Morgans per haplotype, and use the same span consistently for the fraction and for the exposure in the rate estimate. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3374321/

label: Few tracts: high variance and downward bias in t
text: PITFALL: With one individual's genome there are few tracts, so the time estimate has a large variance and a known downward bias, and for very recent admixture (small t) tract lengths are neither exponential nor independent because the pedigree and within-ancestry recombination dominate. CHECK: count uncensored tracts per haplotype; if fewer than about 20, compute a confidence interval for the rate (a Poisson interval on the switch count divided by exposure) and also derive t separately from the A tracts, the B tracts, and the pooled switch rate to see if they agree. IF FOUND: report t from the pooled switch-rate estimator rather than from one ancestry's mean length, state the interval, and do not over-round a point estimate that the data cannot support. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4096373/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9388397/

label: Generation-counting convention off by one
text: PITFALL: The generation convention is ambiguous and can shift the answer by a whole generation: a haplotype transmitted to the focal individual has passed through one meiosis per generation since the pulse, including the meiosis that produced the focal individual, so an estimate of recombination-rate-per-Morgan equals the number of meioses, not necessarily the number of generations as the grader defines it. CHECK: state explicitly which convention is used, and test both (t and t-1 or t+1) against the observed mean tract length to see which is consistent with the ancestry fractions. IF FOUND: adopt the convention in which tracts of ancestry A are exponential with rate t*(1-m) where t is generations since the admixture pulse for that parental haplotype, and say so in the reasoning so the number is interpretable. SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05904 and https://web.stanford.edu/group/pritchardlab/HGbook/ReleaseV1.1/HGBook-V1.1-ch3.2.pdf

label: Estimate per haplotype; label parents last
text: PITFALL: Forcing the two haplotypes to share one admixture time, or pooling both haplotypes' tracts into one likelihood, hides genuinely different parental histories, which is exactly what the task asks to resolve; conversely, labelling parent1 and parent2 before the QC filters are applied can swap the labels because filtering changes each haplotype's A-fraction. CHECK: fit the A-fraction and t independently for each haplotype, then compare the two times and fractions; recompute the A-fractions after every filtering decision and see whether the ordering of the two haplotypes ever changes. IF FOUND: keep per-haplotype estimates, and assign parent1 as the smaller final A-fraction only after all QC is settled, reporting the gap between the two fractions so a near-tie is visible. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9388397/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7449501/

Treating them as complete tracts shortens the mean and inflates t. Per chromosome and haplotype, count the segments that begin at the first called coordinate or end at the last, see what share of the span they hold, and compare boundary with interior tract lengths. Use the censored exponential estimator: rate = (number of uncensored tract ends, that is observed ancestry switches) / (total Morgan span of all tracts of that ancestry, censored ones included). Equivalently, count switches as events and total span as exposure; chromosome ends are not switches.

reason: The task asks for the fraction 'across the called tract span'; the choice of denominator directly sets both fractions and feeds into t.
text: The ancestry-A fraction must be weighted by genetic length (Morgans) over the span actually called. It is not a count of segments, and the denominator is not physical position or the whole chromosome length. The called span can be shorter than the chromosome lengths given in map_info.tsv, and dividing by chromosome length deflates both fractions. For each haplotype, sum segment lengths per chromosome and compare with length_morgan in map_info.tsv to quantify uncalled flanks and interior gaps, and check that both haplotypes cover the same span. Use the sum of retained, called segment lengths in Morgans per haplotype as the denominator, and use that same span as the exposure in the rate estimate for t.
